narrative.overview: Canopy is a compact SwiftUI/AppKit macOS utility. System typography, SF Symbols, real application icons, native menus, and restrained forest-green selection support direct workspace editing. The canvas explains the window arrangement; the desktop strip keeps workspace navigation available when the editor is closed. Extend these existing conventions incrementally.
keyCharacteristics: Native utility chrome and compact controls.
Visible membership, column structure, and selected workspace.
Neutral surfaces with restrained accent and app-color cues.
Explicit window movement, reversible edits, and honest status labels.

rules.name: The Reserved Strip Rule
rules.body: While arrangement is active, place the workspace strip across each display below the menu bar and reserve its height before positioning app frames. In the observed 3440-wide display it occupied (0, 30, 3440, 32); app content began at y=70 with the current gap. These coordinates describe that display, not a universal menu-bar height. Tabs belong to each display's workspaces. Physical multiple-display behavior remains outside the recorded acceptance.

dos: Do preserve system typography, SF Symbols, native menus, and adaptive semantic surfaces.
Do keep column choices, labeled stack targets, selected workspaces, and Apply Grid readable at the attainable minimum.
Do reserve the desktop strip before calculating managed app frames and keep Edit Grids available when the editor closes.
Do distinguish source-derived states, scoped visual review, and real native-window acceptance.
donts: Don't replace native controls with web-style chrome or invent a new visual identity for an incremental editor change.
Don't add Desktop as a grid tile or membership choice.
Don't recreate desktop workspace buttons during ordinary selection updates.
Don't describe 850 × 560 as the minimum total window or claim screenshots were saved when only CUA tool images were observed.
